title: Hearing Louis Armstrong, Jabbo Smith and Johnny Dunn
summary: He first knew Louis behind blues singers; he describes Johnny Dunn's double-time playing and a long thin horn whose name he cannot recall.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: You mentioned Louis. When did you first become aware of him?
Oh, way back. He used to play behind a lot of those Blues singers, you know.
I know.

Yeah, I used to listen to him ...(? )... There was another trumpet player back in those days, too -- Jabbo Smith. And there was one before Louis named Johnny Dunn, who I liked very much at the time. He used to the double-up time thing, you know, like the ...(? )... He'd do it with three majors and then double up the fourth one. [SINGS EXAMPLE] And it looked like every fourth chord he would just...he would double-time, you know. Playing notes that ...(? )... Solo.
Yeah, he did make a lot of records. He did things with the mutes, too.
Yeah. He used to play a lot of those long horns. What did they call them...? ...(? )... Randy King and all those trumpet... Long... I can't think of the name of
Dickenson - 29
this horn. But it's like a trumpet. It's the same thing as a trumpet. Mostly it had a long, thin arm.
One of those long tapered bells?
Yeah. Oh, I forget what they call them.
But it has valves and everything?
Yeah. Well, they didn't have valves on them way back in the days where they used to draw the pictures of angles and things blowing them horns...
Well, bugles...
No, that's not a bugle. This is a long horn. A very long horn. I can't think of the name of it. It has a long ...(? )...
Did you see him, Johnny Dunn?
I saw him on the stage. I didn't know him.
[ETC., FRETS ABOUT TV RECEPTION]
Yeah, he went to Europe, and then he sort of just...you didn't hear much from him.
Who, Johnny Dunn?
Yeah.
